scenes.text: Claude found your signup code hashing passwords with plain SHA two fifty-six. Sounds safe. It isn't.
SHA is built for speed. One gaming GPU tries twenty billion guesses a second.
Worse, identical passwords give identical hashes, so one precomputed table cracks everyone who picked hunter2.
Claude switched to bcrypt, which mixes a random salt into each password. Same password, different hash.
And it's slow on purpose. At work factor twelve, that GPU drops from twenty billion guesses a second to about a thousand.
Fast is the enemy. Salt it, and slow it down.
